result.report:
# Contract Comparison Report — No Documents Provided

Status: No documents received — comparison could not be performed.

What I received
- The input `doc-summaries` array is empty. There are no contract texts, summaries, or section data to compare.

What this means
- I cannot identify or analyze differences between contracts if no source texts are provided.
- I did not fabricate or assume any sections, clauses, or terms. All outputs below are based on the absence of input.

How you can provide documents for comparison
- Provide `doc-summaries` as a JSON array where each element represents one document. Each document object should include at minimum:
  - id or name (string) — unique identifier or title of the contract
  - sections (array) — list of section objects, each with:
    - section-name (string)
    - text (string) — the full text of that section
- Example structure:
  [
    {
      "id": "Contract A",
      "title": "Master Services Agreement A",
      "sections": [
        {"section-name": "Term", "text": "This agreement starts..."},
        {"section-name": "Termination", "text": "Either party may..."},
        ...
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "Contract B",
      "title": "Master Services Agreement B",
      "sections": [
        {"section-name": "Term", "text": "This agreement commences..."},
        {"section-name": "Termination", "text": "Either party may terminate..."},
        ...
      ]
    }
  ]
- Alternatively, paste the full contract texts and I will canonicalize into sections (note: more accurate if you identify sections).

What I will produce after you supply documents
- A Markdown comparison report highlighting overall differences and risks.
- Per-section diffs with a difference summary and significance rating (major/minor/identical).
- High-level key differences with impact analysis.
- A concise executive summary.

Suggested next steps
1. Resubmit with the `doc-summaries` array populated (see structure above).
2. If you prefer, paste or upload the two full contract texts; I can split into sections and then compare.
3. Tell me any priorities (e.g., focus on Indemnity, Liability cap, Termination, IP ownership) so I can prioritize high-risk clauses.

If you send the documents now, I’ll run a detailed, section-by-section comparison and produce the structured ComparisonResult.
